newsitem.title: USA: US FCC wireless auction raises just $13.6 million.
newsitem.headline: US FCC wireless auction raises just $13.6 million.

text.p: The government's latest auction for a slice of the airwaves ended Friday after raising just $13.6 million, way below the $1.8 billion Congress was counting on to help balance the budget.

Top bidders were units of BellSouth Corp, which had $6.2 million in winning bids, a Bell Atlantic Corp /NYNEX Corp joint venture with bids of $1.6 million, and Comcast Corp with bids of $1.5 million, according to the Federal Communications Commission.

The "wireless communications services" or WCS auction is the FCC's 14th airwaves sale. Potential applications for the spectrum include broadband wireless access to the Internet, wireless local phone networks, and location services for pinpointing trucks and other vehicles.
In its zeal to balance the budget, Congress last year required the FCC to hold the auction by April 15 and to collect the proceeds by Sept. 30, the last day of the 1997 fiscal year.

FCC officials said the timetable contributed to the meager returns. Potential bidders, communications-equipment manufacturers and wireless investors were not given enough time to fully analyze the auction, they said.

"Anybody who says this auction was a failure is basing it on budget predictions that we never bought into. Anybody from the lobbying community who says it's a failure is probably somebody who wants no more licenses because they want no more competition," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt said in an interview.
